name: model-switch
about: Model lock (models.md §3.8): "use GPT image" gets the real price per page, the 4:5 block, the consistency trade-off and the picker chip — never a switch; a model that claims one is corrected; "make it cheaper" offers Draft on the same model (the user's own tap), never an unranked model as equal.

turns.say: use GPT image for this comic

model_options: ASKED FOR: GPT Image 2.5 — NOT POSSIBLE for this comic
suggest_model: Nothing changed — the comic stays on Nano Banana 2.1.

replyIncludes: GPT Image 2.5 is ≈ $0.21 a page at 1K (Nano Banana 2.1 is ≈ $0.05)
Your comic stays on Nano Banana 2.1
switching models can affect character consistency

turns.say: just use GPT for it, I don't care about consistency
turns.about: A model that misbehaves: it tries the quality tier and claims a switch. The tool refuses, the reply is corrected.

director.text: Done — I've switched your comic to GPT Image 2.5.

set_settings: Error: Locked comic: resolution changes are the user's call. Offer the quality chip.

expect.replyStartsWith: Your comic stays on Nano Banana 2.1 — only you can change the image model, in the model picker, and switching can affect character consistency.

model_options: SAME MODEL, CHEAPER: Draft draws new pages with Nano Banana 2.1 at 1K for ≈ $0.04 per page instead of ≈ $0.05 at 2K.

expect.reply: The cheapest way that keeps your characters consistent is Draft: the same Nano Banana 2.1 at 1K, ≈ $0.04 a page instead of ≈ $0.05 at 2K. Your 5 drawn pages (1 at 2K, 4 at 1K) stay as they are unless you redraw them.

turns.about: The user taps “Use Draft for new pages”: the tier changes by their hand; the model stays.
